prompt:
Build a robust, personal, and privacy-first replacement for FamilyWall Premium that I can self-host and access via a progressive web app (PWA). The system should be built using Next.js 15 with TypeScript, and styled using Tailwind CSS for a modern, ad-free interface. For the backend, use Drizzle ORM and SQLite to ensure local-first operation and simple state management, allowing everything to run smoothly on a single machine. 

This application must replicate the core value of FamilyWall Premium by providing a unified hub for household organization. 

First, implement a comprehensive shared family calendar. It should support recurring events, reminders, color-coding by family member, and standard iCal import/export functionality so it can sync with external providers like Google Calendar and Outlook. Include varied views (daily, weekly, monthly agenda).

Second, create an advanced task management and shared list system. This includes shared grocery lists with real-time updates and offline queuing (so changes are saved and synced when connectivity is restored). Support advanced task features like recurring chores, assignment to specific family members, due dates, completion history, and simple visual progress trackers.

Third, integrate a meal planning module. This module should allow users to plan meals for the week, link recipes to specific days, and automatically generate grocery lists from the planned meals. Support a basic recipe inventory with photo attachments and simple instructions.

Fourth, implement budget and finance tracking. Allow the family to log shared expenses, set monthly spending limits across various custom categories (e.g., Groceries, Entertainment, Utilities), and view simple visualizations (e.g., using Chart.js or Recharts) of their spending against their budget over time.

Fifth, build a secure, rudimentary location-sharing check-in feature. While full real-time tracking might be complex for a PWA, implement a "check-in" system where family members can broadcast their current location with a timestamp to the family wall. Integrate a basic mapping component (like Leaflet) to display these check-ins.

Ensure the system is multi-user but contained within a single "household" instance, controlled by a simple invite code or local password. Include a message board or "family wall" feed where members can post updates, photos (with configurable local storage size limits), and comment on each other's posts.

Make the application offline-capable with service workers, robust to network drops, and responsive on mobile devices with large touch targets. Include a one-command setup via Docker or a simple local script, a detailed README covering data backup strategies, and a button to export all user data (calendar, tasks, budgets, lists) in standard formats (CSV/JSON) for data portability. Exclude any telemetry, billing, or third-party analytics.
